elements.text:
Terminology

Broker: The servers that hold the queue

Partition: The "queue". An ordered, immutable sequence of message
that we append to, like a log file. Each broker can have multiple
partitions

Topic: A logical grouping of partitions. You publish to and consume
from topics in kafka.

Producers: Write messages to topic

Consumers: Read messages off of topics

stream. Frankly, the distinction here is minor. In both modes,

elements.text:
What happens when a consumer goes down?

1. Just read the latest offset, committing the offset
    When the consumer goes down, kafka consumer reads from the last commit

2. If a consumer group, rebalance it reads till the offset and go ahead
    if one consumer goes down, Kafka will redistribute the partitions
among the remaining consumers so that all partitions are still being
processed.

by the consumer and push it to retry topic
with N retries

Retention Policy

Two settings

1. retention.ms ( default 7 days ) - how long to keep a message
2. retention.bytes ( default 1 GB ) - when to start purging based on size

elements.text:
Kafka consumers work on pull-based model.

This pull-based has many advantages
- Consumption rate
- simplifies failure handling
- prevents overwhelming slow consumers
- efficient batching
